spans.s:
21. Śroṇā, ‘lame,’ or śravaṇa, ‘ear,’ denotes the bright star Aquilæ with below and above it. Weber very need lessly thinks that the name śravaṇa suggested two ears and the head between. It is quite out of correspondence with the Manāzil and the Sieou, and is clearly an Indian invention.
Foot notes Op. cit., 2, 382; but see Whitney, 404.
Oldenberg, loc. cit.

Śrotriya in the Atharvaveda and later denotes a ‘Brahmin learned in holy lore,’ ‘theologian.’
Foot notes ix. 6, 37; x. 2, 20 et seq.
kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xxiii. 4; xxviii. 4; aitareya brāhmaṇa, i. 25, 15; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, v. 4, 4, 5; xiii. 4, 3. 14; taittirīya upaniṣad, ii. 8, etc. Cf. mahā-śrotriya, ‘a great theologian,’ in Chāndogya upaniṣad, v. 11, 1.
